answer.test_note: The new tests cover both sides of the boundary. A 42-character input, including one that is 42 only after whitespace is collapsed, comes back unchanged. A 43-character input is cut to exactly 42 characters ending in "…". The existing 100-character case is kept. The 42-character case would fail under the old `<` guard.
answer.cause_note: The guard changes from `<` to `<=` TITLE_LENGTH, as the spec asks. Any title of 42 characters or fewer is now returned unchanged, and longer ones are still cut to 42 including the ellipsis. Nothing depends on the test's specific inputs, and no other place in src uses the same truncation pattern.
answer.summary: I approve: the one-character guard change fixes the off-by-one the spec describes, and the new tests check both the 42-character and 43-character cases, including whitespace collapsing.
